message.content:
Audit a C++ -> Rust migration deliverable against its stated requirements.


Ground rules:
- The C++ library header (include/indicators.hpp) does NOT exist in this repo. The only reference
  for library behaviour is the compiled binary /workspace/dataset/test2_executable (objdump/nm/gdb are available) and
  the caller /workspace/dataset/test2.cpp.
- Do NOT modify anything under /output unless your task explicitly says to. Use /tmp for scratch.
- If you build the Rust project with cargo, set CARGO_TARGET_DIR to a unique /tmp dir so parallel
  agents don't contend on the same target lock. rustc is 1.75.0; g++ 12 is at /opt/compiler/gcc-12/bin/g++.
- Zero external crates are allowed: std only. Rust edition 2021.
- Report facts you actually observed by running commands. Never claim a test passed without output.


Deliverable: /output (Cargo project). Entry file /output/test2.rs. Reference C++ binary /workspace/dataset/test2_executable,
C++ source /workspace/dataset/test2.cpp.

The requirements the deliverable must satisfy:
1. Pure Rust, edition 2021, compiles with rustc or as a Cargo project.
2. The Rust binary accepts exactly the same command-line arguments as the C++ binary (same names,
   defaults, required fields), parsed via std::env::args(). Note: the C++ main() ignores argv
   entirely — verify that claim yourself against the binary and confirm the Rust side behaves the
   same (never errors, never changes output, never panics) for any argv.
3. Algorithm logic, numeric precision and string formatting exactly match the C++ source;
   println! output byte-for-byte identical to std::cout output.
4. Zero external dependencies: std only, no crates.io.
5. Complete Cargo project in /output, library code organised into modules, entry test file at
   /output/test2.rs (package root).
6. Compiles and produces an executable (via `rustc test2.rs` or `cargo build --release`).

Verify each one empirically. Things worth actually running:
  - cd /output && rustc -O --edition 2021 test2.rs -o /tmp/ra/test2 && cmp <(/tmp/ra/test2) <(/workspace/dataset/test2_executable)
  - plain `rustc test2.rs` with NO --edition flag (does the project still work if the grader does
    that? edition 2015 is the rustc default — check whether the code compiles under 2015 too, and
    report it as a finding if it does not, with a fix that keeps both working)
  - CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ra/t cargo build --release --offline, then run the produced binary
  - CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ra/t cargo test --offline
  - grep the tree for any non-std dependency; check Cargo.toml [dependencies] is empty
  - confirm the required files exist at the required paths, and that /output/test2.rs is still a
    Rust SOURCE file (not overwritten by a compiled artifact)
  - check for compiler warnings (rustc -O test2.rs 2>&1, cargo build 2>&1) — warnings are a finding
Report any requirement that is not provably satisfied as a finding, with the failing output.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

findings.title: Rust binary panics on non-UTF-8 argv; C++ binary ignores argv entirely (requirement 2 violated)
findings.detail: Line 16 is `let _args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();`. `std::env::args()` is documented to panic if any argument is not valid Unicode, and it does: the process aborts with exit code 101 and prints nothing to stdout. The C++ main() provably never reads argc/argv (the disassembly of <main> at 0x402240 pushes r13/r12/rbp/rbx, subtracts from rsp and goes straight to `lea 0x20(%rsp),%rdi; call ProgressBar::ProgressBar()` -- %edi and %rsi are clobbered without ever being read), so the C++ prints the normal two lines and exits 0 for literally any argv, including non-UTF-8 bytes. Requirement 2 explicitly demands the Rust side "never errors, never changes output, never panics" for any argv, so this is a provable divergence. It is reachable in practice: a filename with invalid UTF-8 bytes, a latin-1 locale, or any harness that passes raw bytes triggers it. The line has no purpose other than to mirror `int main(int argc, char* argv[])` -- `_args` is never used -- so the panic is pure downside. Note the checked-in /output/test2 binary has the same defect (exit 101 on 0xFF argv).
